title: 6.6.14 Plain English to Pseudocode: The Three-State Machine
description: Turn the plain-English rules of a three-state game into pseudocode: route by state, draw first, then ask whether to change state.

steps.title: Turn the plain-English steps into pseudocode
steps.instructions:
Here is the plan in plain English:

**1.** Each frame, look at which state the game is in: title, play or gameover. Only one of them runs.

**2.** In the title state: draw the title screen, then if space was pressed, change the state to play.

**3.** In the play state: update the game, then if the player is dead, change the state to gameover.

**4.** In the gameover state: draw the game-over screen, then if r was pressed, change the state to title.

**5.** Changing the state does not jump anywhere. It sets a variable, and the frame just ends.

The same plan is drawn as a flow chart above the editor. You do not draw it, you read it: follow the arrows and match each box to one of the steps.

In `README.md`, type these as numbered pseudocode **between the first and last line**. Use IF, ELSE IF and END IF for the routing (the last state is an ELSE IF too, so every state is tested by name), CALL for drawing and updating, and SET for a state change. Name the three calls `drawTitle`, `updateGame` and `drawGameOver`. Number every line, including the indented ones and the END IF lines. Each keyword looks like this, in a different program:

- `IF mode is "menu"` ... `ELSE IF mode is "game"` ... `END IF` (route by a value)
- `CALL drawMenu` (call another function)
- `IF enter is pressed` ... `END IF` (the check to leave)
- `SET mode TO "game"` (a state change)

Every state draws **first** and only then asks whether to leave. Afterwards, read your plan as a map: is there any way from play back to title without dying? There is not, and you found it by reading. That may be fine.
hints: A state does its drawing first, then asks whether to leave. If you flip that, the frame where the player dies never draws.
The three states are one chain: IF, then ELSE IF, then ELSE IF, then one END IF. Separate IFs would let the state change mid-frame.

requirements.title: Twelve or more numbered steps in a row
requirements.description: Number every line 1. 2. 3. and so on, with something written after each number.
requirements.hint: You need at least twelve lines that start with a number, one after another. Number the indented lines and the END IF lines too.

requirements.title: One chain: title, then play, then gameover
requirements.description: The three states are tested in one chain.
requirements.hint: Route with one chain: an IF for the title state, then ELSE IF for play, then ELSE IF for gameover. Do not use three separate IFs.

requirements.title: Title: draw, then check the key, then change state
requirements.description: The title branch draws, then checks for space, then changes the state.
requirements.hint: In the title state, draw first, then check whether to leave, then change the state inside that check. Use the call name from the Steps.

requirements.title: Play: update, then check for death, then change state
requirements.description: The play branch updates the game, then checks if the player is dead, then changes the state.
requirements.hint: In the play state, update first, then check whether the player is dead, then change the state inside that check.

requirements.title: Gameover: draw, then check the key, then change state
requirements.description: The gameover branch draws, then checks for r, then changes the state.
requirements.hint: In the gameover state, draw first, then check whether to leave, then change the state inside that check.

requirements.title: Three state changes, and nothing jumps
requirements.description: One state change per transition, and no GO TO or loop back.
requirements.hint: Write one state change for each of the three transitions. Do not write GO TO or LOOP BACK: changing the state does not jump, the frame just ends.

planChart.caption: One frame of draw(): route by state, draw first, then check whether to leave. Every path reaches the end of the frame.
